fixes.title: Sequence header reports '0 frames' for a Science Photometry node that says '60 frames', and pre-flight claims 'No exposure nodes found'
fixes.summary: Two of the three surfaces were already closed by an earlier wave and carry tests (packages/skotiq_core/test/providers/sequence/science_photometry_counts_as_exposure_test.dart): Sequence._countExposures and _estimateNodeIntegration now fold SciencePhotometryNode in (so the toolbar chip, which reads sequence.totalExposures at sequence_toolbar/actions_and_estimate.dart:143, is correct), and NoExposuresRule no longer fires on a photometry-only sequence. The surface still lying was plan_math.dart's plannedCaptureUnder — the SHARED walk behind the target header card (target_header_card.dart:673) and the sequence library card preview (sequence_card.dart:464/520) — which knew only ExposureNode and SmartExposureNode. A photometry-only target therefore read 'No exposures' on its own card while the node row beneath it said '60 frames'. Added the SciencePhotometryNode branch: frames += count * mult, integration += exposureSecs * count * mult, filed under the node's own photometric band.
fixes.revert_check: Deleted the `} else if (node is SciencePhotometryNode) {` branch (plan_math.dart lines 105-113) — 3 of the 4 tests failed (frames 0 != 60, integration 0.0 != 3600.0, byFilter {} != {'V': 3600.0}); restored and all 4 pass.
fixes.caveats: The '0m' half of the original report was already false when verified — the verifier corrected it (SequenceTimeEstimator has handled SciencePhotometryNode since sequence_time_estimator.dart:618). The stale walk was Sequence.estimateIntegrationSecs, now fixed.

fixes.title: The daylight gate blocks light frames only when a Target node is present — a targetless Take Exposures wrote 3 daylight LIGHT frames
fixes.summary: Already closed by an earlier wave and already covered by a test. execute_exposure_with_renderer (native/skotiq_native/sequencer/src/instructions.rs:2161-2204) now gates on frame_type_requires_darkness(&config.frame_type) alone; whether the rig is pointed at the sky is answered by ctx.device_ops.mount_is_parked, which is the real discriminator. The old `&& ctx.target_ra.is_some() && ctx.target_dec.is_some()` conjunct is gone. Test `untargeted_light_exposure_rejected_when_sun_up` (instructions.rs:10484) pins it. I added a duplicate test before spotting the existing one and removed it again — instructions.rs is byte-identical to its pre-visit state.
fixes.revert_check: Re-added the two `ctx.target_ra.is_some() && ctx.target_dec.is_some()` conjuncts to the `if frame_type_requires_darkness(...)` condition at instructions.rs:2172. untargeted_light_exposure_rejected_when_sun_up FAILED with 'got Some("Completed 1 exposures")' — i.e. the targetless daylight LIGHT burst captured. Restored; 3 pass.
fixes.caveats: Verified against the exposure path only; the slew half of the gate (instructions.rs:996) was never target-presence-keyed.

fixes.title: 'Wait for Time' with no time picked returns Success instantly — a silent no-op with no validation warning
fixes.summary: Two halves. RUNTIME half was already closed by an earlier wave: execute_wait_time (native/skotiq_native/sequencer/src/instructions.rs:6540-6549) now returns InstructionResult::failure('Wait node has no wait condition: set a target time or a twilight condition') instead of success, covered by an existing Rust test. PRE-FLIGHT half was still open exactly as the finding named it — timing_rules.dart:17 `if (waitUntil == null) continue;` meant an unconfigured node produced NO ValidationIssue, and grep confirmed WaitTimeNode appears in no other rule. Added WaitTimeUnconfiguredRule: ValidationSeverity.error when an enabled WaitTimeNode has neither waitUntil nor waitForTwilight. Errors block start (preflight_validation_dialog.dart:1191 leaves onPressed null when hasErrors), so the run cannot begin with a wait that cannot wait. Also added the sibling the finding's proposed_fix named: LoopUntilTimeUnsetRule, error when an untilTime LoopNode has no repeatUntil — loop_node.rs:85-93 evaluates UntilTime against condition_value and returns should_continue=false when it is None, so the loop body never runs once, and neither LoopEndTimePastRule (skips null) nor UnboundedLoopRule (only forever/whileDark) covered it. Both registered in defaultSequenceValidators.
fixes.revert_check: Deleted the two registration lines `WaitTimeUnconfiguredRule(),` and `LoopUntilTimeUnsetRule(),` from defaultSequenceValidators (sequence_validation.dart:310-311) — i.e. severed the WIRING, leaving the rule classes intact. Both 'registered in the pre-flight registry' tests failed (validateSequence produced no blocking issue). Restored; 9/9 pass.
fixes.caveats: A Wait node dropped from the palette starts unconfigured, so it now shows a blocking pre-flight error until the operator sets a time or twilight condition. That is the finding's stated expectation and matches what the runtime already does (fail rather than instantly succeed).

fixes.title: Every node failure is listed twice in the Session Report and raised as two identical toasts
fixes.summary: One root cause with three layers. (1) RETRY inflation (the 6x/7x dome case) was already closed by an earlier wave: log_and_get_status_with_context (instructions.rs:497) now publishes InstructionFailed only on the first attempt, gated by !is_disconnect_retry_attempt(). (2) The 2x duplication is structural: the executor's terminal handler drains the broadcast buffer for the last InstructionFailed and re-formats it byte-for-byte as SequenceFailed.error (executor/mod.rs:858 last_instruction_failure), so Dart receives the SAME string twice — once as SequencerEvent.Error, once as SequencerEvent.Failed. The Session Report half is closed by SequenceRunStats.recordTerminalError + _recordTerminalRunError on the three terminal call sites in sequence_executor.dart (876/895/909); that landed in the working tree while I was working and I added the wiring test it lacked. (3) The TOAST/banner half was still fully open and is my fix: both payload variants are on the isCriticalEvent allow-list (event_display.dart:115/120) and skotiqEventDisplayDetail returns the same string for both, so runDashboardCriticalEventsBridgeProvider escalated one failed node as two identical 'Critical · Sequencer' toasts, two identical banner rows and (when enabled) two pushes. Added a per-run ledger of already-escalated mid-run reasons and _isRestatedFailureReason: a terminal Failed whose reason text this run already announced is skipped. Matching on the reason text rather than a time window is what keeps a genuinely new terminal reason escalating, and the ledger clears on SequencerEvent.Started so the next run failing the same way is news again. Needed SequencerEvent_Failed added to the bridge_events export show-list (it was the only Sequencer variant missing).
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/sequencer/widgets/run_dashboard/terminal_failure_not_double_escalated_test.dart (4 tests) + packages/skotiq_core/test/providers/sequence/terminal_error_not_recorded_twice_test.dart (3 tests, drives the real executor event handler via handleSequencerEventForTest)
fixes.revert_check: Toast half: deleted the `if (_isRestatedFailureReason(...)) continue;` call site in the bridge loop (the production wiring, leaving the helper). 2 of 4 tests failed — banner had 2 RunDashboardEvents for one failed node. Restored; 4/4 pass and the pre-existing critical_events_bridge_test.dart 7/7 still pass. Report half: replaced all three `_recordTerminalRunError(error)` calls in sequence_executor.dart with `_recordRunError(error)`. 'one failed node produces one error entry, not two' failed; restored, 3/3 pass.
fixes.caveats: The Session Report half was authored by a concurrent agent in the same working tree (sequence_stats_provider.dart / sequence_executor.dart / event_operations.dart, mtimes 23:18-23:21); I verified it, added the missing wiring test, and left their code untouched. Their dedupe compares only errorMessages.last, which is correct for the observed adjacency but would still double-record if an unrelated error landed between the mid-run and terminal event.

fixes.title: Pre-flight warns 'Slew to Target scheduled at 12:47 before target rises at 03:41'
fixes.summary: Already closed by an earlier wave, with a test, and I confirmed the test is load-bearing. Root cause was that TargetWindow.isVisibleAt tested membership of the solved rise/set INTERVAL: the solver scans one local-noon-to-noon window, so a target already up at the anchor has no rise inside its own visible interval and what comes back is the NEXT night's rise — every membership test then answers 'not up yet' for a target at the zenith. TargetWindow now carries the geometry it was solved from (raDeg/decDeg/latitudeDeg/longitudeDeg/minAltitudeDeg, sequence_time_estimator.dart:103-130) and isVisibleAt asks the sky directly via altitudeAt() >= minAltitudeDeg, falling back to the interval only for fixture-built windows with no geometry. The end-of-node 'after target sets' check gained the same !isVisibleAt(end) guard, and boundary instants on another calendar day now print '03:41 on 06-16' via _formatTimeRelativeTo so a bare time can no longer read as already-past.
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_core/test/services/sequence_time_estimator_visibility_test.dart (4 tests) — it searches for a real date on which the reported shape occurs in the host timezone, so it is not tied to a fixture
fixes.revert_check: Deleted the `final altitude = altitudeAt(time); if (altitude != null) return altitude >= (minAltitudeDeg ?? 0);` block from TargetWindow.isVisibleAt (sequence_time_estimator.dart:151-154), restoring the interval test. 2 of 4 failed ('a target at the zenith is not reported as "before target rises"' and 'isVisibleAt answers from the sky, not from the reported interval'). Restored; the visibility suite plus the pre-existing sequence_time_estimator_test.dart pass 40/40 together.
fixes.caveats: None — the pre-existing estimator suite (including its four isVisibleAt cases built from bare rise/set fixtures) still passes, so the geometry-less fallback path is intact.

fixes.title: The Collapse button blanks the whole sequence tree to an empty grey rectangle
fixes.summary: Already closed by an earlier wave, with a test, and I confirmed the test is load-bearing. Root cause in node_tree_view.dart: the collapsed-container branch reassigned `Widget headerRow` to a DragTarget whose builder CLOSURE then read `headerRow` — a closure captures the variable, not the value it held when written, so the row became its own descendant and every build nested another DragTarget -> AnimatedContainer -> DragTarget. Only collapsed containers took that branch, which is exactly why the grey block appeared on Collapse and vanished on Expand. The fix makes the row `final Widget baseRow`, introduces a separate `Widget headerRow = baseRow`, and has the builder return `baseRow`.
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/sequencer/sequence_tree_collapse_all_test.dart (2 tests) — asserts the container headers and top-level siblings are still rendered AND hit-testable after Collapse all (a tap on the tail row must select it, which a covering grey block would swallow), and that Expand all restores the hidden rows
fixes.revert_check: Restored the pre-fix shape exactly: `Widget headerRow = SequenceTreeContextMenu(...)`, removed `Widget headerRow = baseRow;`, and pointed the DragTarget builder's child back at `headerRow`. The test run then NEVER COMPLETED — zero test results in 15 minutes, killed by the 900s timeout, because the element tree nests without bound. Restored the fix; both tests pass in 8s.
fixes.caveats: The revert signal is a hang rather than an assertion failure, which is the honest shape of this defect (unbounded nesting); in a release build Flutter substitutes ErrorWidget for the throwing subtree, which is the bare grey rectangle the auditor photographed.
